**My reasoning as this farmer:**

I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over 40 years. The North China Plain has one rhythm that every farmer here knows in their bones: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same plot. That rotation is what I will do again this year — there is no serious alternative on my land.

I farm 15 mu. The soil here is silty loam, decent but demanding on irrigation. Groundwater has been dropping for years. I've seen the researchers from China Agricultural University come through — I've attended the technical meetings at the county extension office. I know we've been over-applying nitrogen for decades, and I've been pulling back on my N rates gradually. I don't need to chase the maximum yield at any cost; I need a stable, profitable harvest that doesn't degrade my soil for the next decade.

For wheat, I'll use a certified improved variety — Jimai 22 has been reliable in this county. I'll use rotary tillage to incorporate the previous maize stover. I'll split my nitrogen: base application before planting, topdress at jointing. Three irrigation events: pre-sowing, jointing, and heading. Rust and aphids are the main threats — I'll spray twice.

For maize, I'll go straight to no-tillage direct seeding right after wheat harvest in June. Zhengdan 958 is my hybrid of choice — stable performer under our conditions. Only one planned irrigation at sowing if the soil is dry; summer rainfall usually covers the rest. One pesticide pass for corn borer.
